ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
Some health professionals suspect that doctors are more likely to order cardiac tests for men than women, even when women describe exactly the same symptoms. Young doctors, training to work in the emergency room, were randomly assigned to two groups-Group A and Group B-and presented with the exact same description of common symptoms of heart disease. However, those in Group A were told that the patient was a 55-year-old female and those in Group B were told that the patient was a 55-year-old male. All other patient characteristics were exactly the same. Which of the following is the appropriate statistic to test whether doctors are less likely to order cardiac tests when the patient is female?

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: In the image is a two-row data table: the number of doctors in Group A is 60, the number who ordered the standard heart examination is 42, and the proportion is 70%; the number of doctors in Group B is 40, the number who ordered the standard heart examination is 34, and the proportion is 85%. The problem statement explains that Group A corresponds to a patient who is a 55-year-old female, and Group B corresponds to a patient who is a 55-year-old male. To test whether doctors are less likely to order a heart examination under the female patient condition, therefore the direction of the difference should be set as the female proportion minus the male proportion, namely \hat p_F-\hat p_M=0.70-0.85. Under the null hypothesis p_F=p_M, the two-proportion z test uses the pooled proportion. The pooled proportion is (42+34)/(60+40)=76/100=0.76, and the complement proportion is 0.24. Therefore the standard error is sqrt((0.76)(0.24)(1/60+1/40)), so the appropriate z statistic is z=(0.70-0.85)/sqrt((0.76)(0.24)(1/60+1/40)).

Young doctors, training to work in the emergency room, were randomly assigned to two groups—Group A and Group B—and presented with the exact same description of common symptoms of heart disease. However, those in Group A were told that the patient was a 55-year-old female and those in Group B were told that the patient was a 55-year-old male. method.method_draft: Read the table in the image: Group A has 60 doctors and 70% ordered cardiac tests; Group B has 40 doctors and 85% ordered cardiac tests. From the text, map Group A to the female patient condition and Group B to the male patient condition. Since the question asks whether doctors are less likely to order tests for the female patient, set the statistic in the direction female minus male: \(\hat p_F-\hat p_M=0.70-0.85\). Use the two-proportion z test under \(H_0:p_F=p_M\), so the standard error uses the pooled proportion. Compute the pooled proportion from the table counts: \((42+34)/(60+40)=0.76\), with complement \(0.24\). Substitute into \(z=(\hat p_F-\hat p_M)/\sqrt{\hat p(1-\hat p)(1/n_F+1/n_M)}\), giving \(z=\frac{0.70-0.85}{\sqrt{(0.76)(0.24)(1/60+1/40)}}\).
